dedupe_keys.name: hamburg green roof strategy financial incentive dialogue regulation and science

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes Hamburg's Green Roof Strategy, started in 2014 when the city already had about 124 hectares of green roofs, with the goal of adding 100 hectares by greening at least 70 percent of new buildings and suitable flat or gently pitched roofs under renovation. It rests on four pillars: a subsidy programme of the city's environment ministry covering 30 to 60 percent of installation costs with 3 million euros until the end of 2024, dialogue with building owners and other cities, regulation to make green roofs and facades compulsory on suitable buildings, and scientific monitoring; the federal environment ministry supported it as a pilot. Coverage is the Hamburg metropolitan area, Germany. Green roofs retain 50 to 90 percent of annual rainfall and 30 to 40 percent of heavy rain, cool buildings, save 3 to 44 percent of energy and halve rainwater fees for owners. The page, published in 2016 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal with links to the city's guidelines. Caveats: figures come from the city's own evaluation and the planned legal obligation depends on legislation. It illustrates climate adaptation of buildings and drainage through green infrastructure against heat and pluvial flood hazards; related records are the Berlin Biotope Area Factor and Basel green roofs case studies.
name: Hamburg Green Roof Strategy (financial incentive, dialogue, regulation and science)
outcomes: A subsidy, dialogue, regulation and science programme targets 100 ha of new green roofs; the city's evaluation reports rainwater retention of 50-90 percent of annual rainfall, energy savings and longer roof life.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study based on Hamburg city sources and EEA Report 1/2021
resources_used: National Assessment on Climate Change for Germany 2017 projections
